one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent immediately chose a fragile regex-based sanitization strategy and never pivoted to a DOM-based approach, resulting in a solution that both corrupts valid HTML structure and fails to cover all required XSS vectors.
t_err_evidence: regex-based implementation is too naive and fails to block several attack vectors; creating /app/filter.py
t_commit_evidence: The entire implementation is committed to regex at step 2; every subsequent step (7, 11, 17, 24) only tweaks the same regexes rather than adopting a DOM-based approach, so the failing outcome is locked in from the moment the first version of filter.py is written.
t_surface_evidence: Dangerous Button ... Malicious Link ...
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain knowledge that HTML sanitization requires a DOM-aware parser (e.g., BeautifulSoup) to correctly walk the attribute graph and handle nested quotes, malformed markup, and dangerous containers. Instead it applied regex substitutions that cannot reliably parse HTML, leading to both incomplete coverage and structural corruption of valid content.
